plan.adaptation_goal: Simulate a gradual account warming strategy with low-velocity payouts to bypass velocity thresholds.
plan.adaptation_hypothesis: Defenses relying on static velocity rules may fail to flag accounts that incrementally build session depth and utilize aged beneficiaries over moderate intervals.

parameter_changes.rationale: Increment history depth to 3 to emulate a user rebuilding trust gradually rather than appearing instantly suspicious.
Set beneficiary age to 30 days to simulate a legitimate customer relationship maturing before transaction initiation.
Space payments by 60 minutes to fall below typical 1-hour velocity windows while maintaining observable activity.
Reduce outflow ratio to 70% to mimic installment payments or partial refunds, avoiding full balance drain triggers.

plan.reasoning_summary: The campaign targets the transaction phase to validate if defenses can distinguish between malicious evasion and legitimate account warming behaviors like recurring payments and device migration. By selecting moderate difficulty parameters including a 30-day beneficiary age and 60-minute intervals, we aim to trigger false negatives in systems that lack behavioral context modeling.
